The Deloitte Master's Thesis Hub bridges bright students with unanswered questions Deloitte is curious about.

The program is a great place to meet like-minded students navigating the ups and downs of thesis writing. Best of all, you'll have the invaluable opportunity to get guidance and support during the writing process and tap into the expertise of Deloitte's thought leaders, who will guide you on the path of creating an impactful master thesis!

Our Deloitte experts will be able to provide collaboration and guidance within the following five research topics:

• M&A & Strategy

• Sustainability & ESG

• Financial Performance & Reporting

• Digital Transformation & AI

• Organization & Change Management

Deloitte invests in providing relevant business insight and latest industry trends, challenging your thought process, and giving access to a large network of experts in the specific problem domain. We help develop your problem-solving skills and show you tips and tricks to present research findings concisely. Most importantly, the Master's Thesis Hub offers a room for reflection and shared learning between participants and experts.

By applying to the Master’s Thesis Hub, you will commit to attending four dedicated sessions from January – April 2027 for shared learning and pro-level guidance. To round of the Master Thesis Hub we will have a celebration dinner in June 2027, to congratulate you on your new degree. All sessions will be held in the Deloitte office in Copenhagen (Weidekampsgade 6, 2300 Copenhagen S). Note that it is a requirement to attend all sessions physically at the Copenhagen office to be a part of the program.

Are you ready? We are looking forward to receiving your application!

How to apply?

To apply, click "I'm interested" and upload your CV (along with the CVs of your group members if applicable). You will also be asked to answer a few practical questions.

Final deadline for signing up is the 4th of December. You will receive a response regarding your application shortly thereafter.

We look forward to connecting with you!

In Deloitte, you will find passionate, caring people who are curious by nature and striving to evolve. We value our different skills, perspectives and experiences and foster an environment where innovative powers thrive. To us, success is the feeling that the work we are doing will outlast us. The impact we make is not about what we achieve as individuals, but how we enable those around us to be their very best. From professional development to leadership opportunities, we empower our people to be extraordinary by playing to their strengths – because that is how we can make a difference.

Spirii is hiring! We are looking for a Commercial Director to lead our eMSP business.

****About Spirii

****Spirii was founded in Copenhagen in 2019 with one goal: to make EV charging simple. Today, our software helps charge point operators and businesses in more than 22 markets run and grow their charging networks. Since 2024, we have been part of the Edenred Group, which gives us strong support and a close link to company fleets across Europe. Our next chapter is eMSP, and we are looking for the person to lead it.

****Position Overview

****The Commercial Director eMSP will lead Spirii's commercial strategy and execution for our eMobility Service Provider (eMSP) platform across our priority European markets (Denmark/Sweden, Germany, Netherlands, France, and Italy). As part of the sales leadership team, you will build and scale our eMSP business, serving as the commercial counterpart to our Mobility Product Director. This role requires an entrepreneurial leader who can develop new markets, close complex deals with fleet operators and mobility service providers, and establish Spirii as a leading eMSP competitor.

You will build a new dedicated eMSP sales team while collaborating closely with existing regional sales managers who sell eMSP as an adjacency to CPMS, and partnering with product and operations teams to deliver integrated mobility solutions.

****Key Responsibilities

****Commercial Strategy & Leadership

• Develop and execute the commercial strategy for Spirii's eMSP product line across priority markets

• Define market segmentation, go-to-market approach, and competitive positioning for Spirii’s focus markets

• Serve as the commercial voice in eMSP governance, partnering with the Mobility Product Director

• Contribute to product roadmap prioritization based on market insights and customer needs

• Establish revenue targets, pricing strategies, and business models for eMSP offerings

• Report progress, pipeline, and strategic recommendations to the Chief Sales Officer

• Represent Spirii eMSP at industry events, conferences, and with strategic partners

Business Development & Market Intelligence

• Lead business development activities including mapping the eMSP ecosystem and understanding market movements

• Identify and qualify leads across priority European markets

• Build strategic relationships with fleet operators, leasing companies, retailers, and mobility providers

• Lead pursuit of major tenders requiring eMSP capabilities

• Develop partnership strategies with roaming networks, charge point operators, and technology providers

• Monitor competitive landscape and emerging trends in EV roaming and mobility services

• Generate qualified pipeline and convert opportunities to closed deals

Sales Team Leadership & Execution

• Build, lead, and develop a high-performing eMSP BD and sales team

• Personally close complex, strategic eMSP deals with C-level stakeholders

• Enable and support existing regional sales managers on eMSP specifics in their business deals

• Establish sales processes, methodologies, and enablement programs for eMSP

• Develop proposal templates, business cases, and ROI models for eMSP solutions

• Achieve/exceed annual revenue and customer acquisition targets

Cross-Functional Collaboration

• Partner with Mobility Product Director to align commercial needs with product development

• Collaborate with Roaming Operations team on customer success, issue resolution, and support

• Work with Finance on reconciliation processes, margin control, and pricing strategies

• Coordinate with Marketing on product marketing support for launch and go-to-market activities

• Align with Chief Sales Officer and sales leadership on integrated CPMS+eMSP strategies

• Engage with Legal on contract negotiations and deal structuring

• Provide market feedback to inform technical and operational priorities

**Experience:

****Required Qualifications

**

• 8+ years in B2B sales or business development, with at least 3 years in leadership roles

• Proven track record in the EV charging, mobility services, fleet management, or energy sectors

• Experience selling complex SaaS or platform solutions to enterprise customers

• Demonstrated success building and scaling new business lines or products

• Experience operating across multiple European markets (particularly Denmark/Sweden, Germany, Netherlands, France, Italy)

• Track record of consistently achieving/exceeding revenue targets (€3M+ ARR)

**Knowledge & Skills:

**

• Deep understanding of the EV charging ecosystem, including eMSP, CPMS, and roaming protocols (OCPI, OICP)

• Knowledge of fleet electrification trends and fleet operator business models

• Strong commercial acumen with ability to develop pricing strategies and business models

• Excellent stakeholder management and C-level selling skills

• Strategic thinking combined with hands-on execution capability

• Proven ability to build and lead small, high-performing teams

• Proficiency in CRM systems (Salesforce, HubSpot) and sales analytics

**Personal Attributes:

**

• Entrepreneurial mindset with comfort in ambiguity and building from ground up

• Results-driven with strong accountability and ownership

• Collaborative leadership style with ability to work across sales, product, and operations

• Exceptional communication and presentation skills

• Cultural sensitivity and ability to work in diverse, international teams

• Resilience and adaptability in fast-paced, evolving markets

• Strong team player who can enable regional sales managers on eMSP topics

**Languages:

**

• Fluent in English (required)

• Additional European languages (German, French, Dutch, Swedish, Danish, or Italian) highly desirable

**Education:

**

• Bachelor's degree in Business, Engineering, or related field (Master's degree preferred)

****Benefits

• Flexible Work Environment: Enjoy a collaborative, inclusive, and open workplace designed to fit your needs and support work-life balance

• Competitive Package: A competitive salary, an 11% company pension plan, and a comprehensive benefits package

• Time to Recharge: Benefit from 32 paid vacation days (5 weeks + 5 extra) and paid parental leave to focus on what matters most

• Career Growth: Access professional development opportunities and grow your career in a high-impact, high-growth industry

• Stay Energized: Enjoy excellent coffee, tea, free snacks, and subsidized lunches at the office

• Stay Active: Use our Spirii gym and shared company car to keep moving

• Make an Impact: Be part of a team driving the future of sustainable energy while working on meaningful projects

**About Spirii

**Spirii is a full-service e-Mobility provider, offering hardware and software charging solutions to companies in the private and public sector. Spirii recently celebrated its seven-year anniversary as a founded company — though the people at Spirii bring far more extensive experience working with electric cars and charging, and with the development of future transport and energy systems.

Spirii is an equal opportunity employer. We encourage applications from candidates of all backgrounds and experiences. Spirii strives to create an inclusive and diverse workplace, and we encourage all qualified applicants to apply regardless of age, gender, race, sexual/religious orientation, or disability.

Are you passionate about Embedded Linux and eager to make a real impact across industries? Join Prevas as an Embedded Linux Engineer and Consultant, helping our clients navigate technology transitions, ensure product security, and build new embedded solutions for a safer, smarter world. Whether you come from a consultancy background or have experience as a technical leader in product development, this could be your next step.

About the Role: Embedded Linux Engineering & Consulting

As part of our team, you will collaborate with a wide variety of organizations – from global enterprises to innovative startups. Your main focus will be on embedded Linux development, secure firmware, and technical consulting. You will play an essential role in supporting our clients as they develop, update, and secure their embedded systems, particularly in response to evolving security standards and regulations.

Key Responsibilities in Embedded Linux Engineering & Consulting

• 
Design, develop, and optimize embedded Linux software for various hardware platforms.

• 
Work closely with our skilled engineers and customers.

Desirable: Additional Responsibilities

• 
Collaborate on hardware root-of-trust, secure boot, and chain-of-trust implementations.

• 
Assist in system hardening, configuration for security, encryption, and access control mechanisms and embedded patch management.

What We’re Looking For: Skills & Experience in Embedded Linux.

• 
Background in software development and embedded systems, specifically with Linux.

• 
Ability to work with Linux both in user and kernel space.

• 
Experience working with Yocto

• 
Structured, analytical, and reliable approach to problem solving.

• 
Excellent English communication and writing skills, able to convey technical detail concisely and clearly.

Desirable: Additional Skills & Qualifications

• 
Experience in cybersecurity, software lifecycle management, or security architecture (from any industry – embedded, medical, IT, defense, etc.).

• 
Experience working with security standards – e.g. IEC 62443-4-1/2, IEC 81001-5-1, ETSI EN 303 645, EN 18031, ISO 27001.

• 
Hands-on experience with secure software development technologies such as secure bootloaders, encrypted data storage, threat modelling (e.g. STRIDE), and system authentication methods.

Why Join Prevas? Career Growth in Embedded Linux & Consulting

• 
Be part of a dynamic team where you work closely with experts who value problem solving, personal growth, and technical passion.

• 
Opportunities to influence product security strategies in real-world projects.

• 
Work with a great mix of industries and customers – from large corporations to dynamic startups.

• 
Create lasting impact in both products and organizations through your consulting work.

About Prevas: Engineering Excellence in Embedded Linux & Electronics

At Prevas, embedded technology is at our core. Over the last 40 years, we have completed more than 5,000 development projects across software and electronics. We see development as a natural part of life – from idea to product, and from career to personal growth. Our open, inclusive atmosphere provides you with the space to be yourself and develop your ideas, while working across disciplines with dedicated colleagues.

If you share our passion for problem-solving, teamwork, and learning, and you want to help shape the future of embedded systems and secure IoT solutions, we’d love to hear from you.

Contact Us

For more information or an informal conversation about the role, please contact VP Technology Peter Aagaard Kristensen at +45 51 54 33 66. You can also find out more about us on our website and LinkedIn page.

We look forward to welcoming you to Prevas – where every day is a chance to build something great together.

Systematic

Systematic is an international software company headquartered in Aarhus, Denmark, with more than 1,200 employees and 17 offices worldwide.

The company develops mission-critical software for environments where reliability, security and informed decision-making are essential.

Different solutions are used by more than one million users across 50+ countries within Defence, Healthcare, National Security, Critical Infrastructure and Library.

Read more at www.systematic.com

Do you want a role with a clear sense of purpose, working with mission-critical technology that supports defence organisations and their ability to operate, collaborate and make well-informed decisions in complex environments?

Systematic has experienced significant growth in recent years, with the Defence business playing a key role in this development. Increasing international defence investments, growing requirements for data sovereignty and information security, and a continued need for advanced decision-support solutions are creating new opportunities across the market.

As part of this ongoing development, Systematic is strengthening the leadership around its IRIS Suite and Mobile portfolio. As Director, Product Management, you will take overall responsibility for IRIS Suite, SitaWare Frontline, and SitaWare Edge and lead an experienced Product Management team of eight employees, with plans to expand the team further. Your responsibilities include people leadership, product strategy, and the commercial development of the portfolio.

You will set the direction for the portfolio, translate customer and market needs into clear product priorities, and ensure a strong business rationale for future investments and development initiatives. Reporting directly to the Vice President, Product Management, Defence, you will work closely with senior management, technical functions, and commercial teams as well as strategic customers, giving you a central role in key product and investment decisions.

Your main responsibilities will include:

• Execute the strategic direction for the IRIS Suite and Mobile portfolios and translate it into clear product roadmaps and development priorities.

• Drive the commercial development of the portfolio, including business plans, market priorities, and long-term growth opportunities.

• Lead and develop the product management team, taking responsibility for results, competencies, resources, and long-term capacity.

• Prepare business analyses, budgets, and investment proposals, and present recommendations to Product Boards and other relevant decision-making bodies.

• Maintain a close dialogue with customers and operational end-users and translate their needs into product priorities and development initiatives.

• Identify and evaluate new products, features, markets, and business models in collaboration with the innovation department and other relevant stakeholders.

• Work closely with the sales, marketing, and technical departments on strategic customer opportunities, major proposals, and product expansions.

• Monitor the portfolio’s performance and use insights into the market, customers, and the business to adjust priorities and support key product decisions.

Who are you?

You have a relevant degree in engineering, software, computer science, electronics, or a related field such as Business Development Engineering, combining technology with commercial insights.

You bring solid experience from working in a product-driven software company where software is the core business, preferably from a role combining Product Management, commercial responsibility, and leadership. You have proven management experience in building high-performing teams, strong business acumen, and the ability to connect customer needs, product strategy, market opportunities, and investment priorities.

You are not expected to be the leading technical specialist, but you understand complex software products well enough to engage credibly with specialists and make informed product and business decisions.

As a leader, you are pragmatic, curious, and action-oriented. You set a clear direction, build trust, challenge constructively, and give experienced specialists the space to leverage their expertise, while maintaining ownership of key decisions and overall priorities.

You must be able to present a clean criminal record and have lived in a NATO and/or an EU country for the past seven years, as Systematic works with security-classified projects.

Influence the direction of mission-critical software

This position gives you significant influence over the development and prioritisation of a strategically important portfolio within one of Systematic’s key growth areas. You will be closely involved in key product and investment decisions and have the opportunity to shape both the portfolio and the continued development of the product management organisation.

At the same time, you will become part of a well-established international software company with a strong position in the defence sector and long-standing relationships with national defence organisations, NATO, and international partners.

Most importantly, you will work with mission-critical software that supports defence organisations in establishing situational awareness, coordinating operations, and making well-informed decisions across land, air, sea, and joint domains.

If you have any questions about the position, you are welcome to contact Research Consultant Simone Svenningsen on tel. 2616 3704.

Please note that we only need your CV when you apply for the position. Your enquiry will be treated confidentially and will not be passed on without your consent.

The Department of Psychology and Behavioural Sciences invites applications for associate professorships in Psychology. The associate professorships are full-time and permanent positions, starting in June 2027 or as soon as possible subject to mutual agreement. The Department’s educational programme covers the subfields of Social and Personality Psychology, Cognitive Psychology, Developmental Psychology, Pedagogical Psychology, Clinical Psychology and Work and Organizational Psychology. In addition, the Department participates in the Flexible Master’s Programme in Public Leadership Education. 

Applicants will be shortlisted for full assessment based on their qualifications and the Department’s need for broad recruitment across the subfields. Hence, applicants not shortlisted will not receive a full assessment. The Department expects to offer up to four associate professorships. The final number of positions to be filled will depend on the assessment of the applicants.

Job description
The announced associate professorships are permanent positions with research and teaching obligations within the specified fields outlined above. The positions come with 50 % teaching, 40 % research and 10 % administration. The successful candidate is expected to take on responsibility for research leadership in the dedicated field, publish in international peer-reviewed journals, attract external funding, develop courses and methods, participate in the Department's day-to-day activities (lecturing, seminars, workshop collaborations, etc.), undertake supervision of students and PhD students as well as participate in administrative and organizational tasks.

Your qualifications
To be considered for shortlisting, applicants must indicate which specific subfield (and potentially another supplemental subfield) they want to apply within.

Relevant candidates are expected to have published a substantial amount of research at a high international level as well as high-quality teaching within the subfield specified by the applicants.

As the successful candidates must participate in all of the department's main activities, including teaching, examination and administration related to the subfield, non-Danish speaking candidates are required to acquire the necessary language skills within a short period of time (max. 2 years).

Permanent employment as associate professor at Aarhus BSS requires completion of, within a two year period, the supervision course and also the course Online and blended learning provided by Centre for Educational Development at Aarhus University.

The required qualifications are elaborated below:

1. Substantial research production at a high international level
To qualify for the position as associate professor, a substantial research production is required. Publication records can have different profiles and should be evaluated in the context of the relevant subfield(s) and in relation to the applicant’s general academic profile. However, because publication statistics display important information regarding researchers' publication merits, applicants are encouraged to provide relevant publication statistics (e.g. number of peer reviewed publications, h-index, citations etc.).

2. Didactical/pedagogical competences and experiences at a high level, including a positive, written evaluation of these competences
Teaching and supervising students at different levels is a main activity of an associate professor. Applicants must submit a teaching portfolio that describes which teaching activities they have been involved in, explicates how and why these activities have been planned and implemented in the way they have and presents the results of one’s teaching activities (e.g., by way of student comments and evaluations, letters of recommendation etc.). A written evaluation of the candidate´s teaching abilities should be enclosed. Applicants should specify which of the subfields mentioned above (one, or alternatively two), that they consider the most obvious areas for teaching activities. Note further, that applicants for applied fields (i.e., Clinical, Pedagogical, and Work and Organizational psychology) are encouraged to document concrete contact and experiences with the relevant societal profession. 

3. Experiences with organizational management, knowledge sharing with the public and external funding
It is expected that associate professors at The Department of Psychology and Behavioural Sciences are responsible and stimulating capacities in their research fields, in their teaching activities and as a colleague at the department. In the assessment of candidates, it will be evaluated if they have:

• Experience with participating in organizational activities and departmental services
• Experience with societal collaboration and knowledge dissemination 
• Experience from teaching in other areas of relevance for psychology.
• Experience with attracting external funding.
Who we are
The Department of Psychology and Behavioural Sciences is part of Aarhus BSS, Aarhus University – a top 100 university. Aarhus BSS has achieved the triple-crown AACSB, AMBA and EQUIS accreditations.

At the Department of Psychology and Behavioural Sciences, we teach and conduct research into the most significant subject areas of psychology. The department employs around 55-60 academic staff members and 40 PhD students. Our researchers have a strong tradition for collaborating with Danish as well as international researchers from many different academic fields such as health and psychiatry, education, pedagogic, linguistics, philosophy, religious studies, organizational development and management, economics and neuroscience.
For more information about the Department of Psychology and Behavioural Sciences, please visit: http://psy.au.dk/en/

Further information
For further information about the position, please contact Head of department, professor, Jan Tønnesvang, e-mail: jan@psy.au.dk

If you need help uploading your application or have any questions about the recruitment process, please contact HR Coordinator Charlotte Thomsen, tel.: +45 93509350, email: Charlotte@au.dk.

Place of work
Department of Psychology and Behavioural Sciences, Bartholins Allé 11, DK-8000 Aarhus C.

International applicant? 
Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Please find more information here:
https://internationalstaff.au.dk/relocationservice/

Please find more information about research opportunities at Aarhus University here: http://international.au.dk/research/

Terms of employment
Salary and terms of employment are governed by the Cirkulære om overenskomst for akademikere i staten  (in Danish). You will be employed as associate professor at base pay level 4–8 with additional supplements in accordance with the Cirkulære om protokollat om visse ansættelsesvilkår for videnskabeligt personale ved universiteter (in Danish).

The job content and qualification requirements are described in further detail in the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

Application procedure
When you apply for this position it is mandatory to attach the following:

• Application
• Curriculum Vitae. You are encouraged to declare any periods of leave without research activity, including, for example, maternity leave, since your research activities are assessed in relation to your actual research time
• Education (diploma for master's, PhD and possibly higher doctoral degree)
• List of publications (the enclosed publications must be clearly marked on the list of publications)
• Publications. Up to five publications can be included in the application. In the event of several authors the publications must be accompanied by a co-author statement concerning the applicant's share of the collaborative work with the consent of the co-authors. This template may be used for the purpose
• Teaching portfolio. The specific requirements regarding the documentation can be found here
 Materials which cannot be uploaded together with the application may be submitted in five copies to Aarhus BSS HR & PhD, Aarhus University, Bartholins Allé 16, DK-8000 Aarhus C.
 Read more about how to apply for an academic post at Aarhus BSS here

The evaluation process
Shortlisting is applied. This means that an appointment committee (assisted by the chair of the assessment committee) advises the head of department on which applicants possess the qualifications, competencies, experience and potential described above under “Your qualifications”, notably in fields with specific departmental research and teaching needs and in accordance with the faculty’s criteria and guidelines for evaluating candidates to permanent positions.

Through the shortlisting process, the head of department selects the applicants who will receive a thorough assessment of their professional qualifications. The applicants will then be assessed by an expert assessment committee. All applicants will be notified whether or not their application has been shortlisted and forwarded to the assessment committee for evaluation. Shortlisted applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee.

 Please note that the assessment of applicants is based solely on the material received prior to the application deadline.

 Read more about the recruitment process, shortlisting procedure and guidelines for assessment committees here. 

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

Aarhus University
Aarhus University is an academically diverse and research-intensive university with a strong commitment to high-quality research and education and the development of society nationally and globally. The university offers an inspiring research and teaching environment to its 37,000 students (FTEs) and 8,700 employees and has an annual revenue of EUR 1.106 billion. Learn more at www.international.au.dk/

Are you currently studying for a B.Sc. or M.Sc. in Software Engineering, Computer Science, Robotics or another education where software development plays a central role, and want to get hands-on experience applying software engineering in a real production codebase? Do you have experience with C#, object-oriented design or unit testing? Are you curious about how AI is changing the way software is built? Do you want to join a fast-moving R&D team that develops state-of-the-art solutions for highly engaged end-users in a global industry? Then, this internship could be just the thing for you!

About Unicontrol

Unicontrol has revolutionized 3D machine control systems for excavators, wheel loaders and dozers, making it accessible for a wider range of contractors. We have a strong vision of very high usability, and all our products and customers are always connected to our cloud/SaaS solution. Established in 2018, we have been able to gain strong and prominent investors from the robotics industry and we are growing fast. Excavators, wheel loaders and dozers are just the beginning, and we offer a position where you will be a key player in ensuring customers' experience when using our innovative solutions!

About the internship

We are opening an internship position to join our software development team within R&D. Our ambition is to guide and automate earthmoving machines, and you will be part of the team that builds the software running on our machine control systems.

As Software Engineering intern, you will work in our C# codebase, which runs on the Unity framework. Your focus will be on software engineering: writing maintainable code, improving architecture, testing and refactoring.

You will be part of a development team of highly experienced developers who are ready to share best practices and learn from you about new trends and technologies.

Your primary tasks will be

• Design and implement new features in C#
• Refactor and improve existing code for readability, structure and performance
• Explore how AI tools can help us write, review and understand code faster
• Take part in code reviews and our Pull Request process
• Debug and fix issues found in testing or reported from the field
• Use agile development tools like Git/Jira/Bitbucket
Your profile

You have a solid foundation in software engineering, with a passion for writing good code and a drive to solve complex challenges. Ideally, you already have programming experience from study projects, personal hobby projects or similar.

You have the drive to learn quickly and can push things forward by yourself. You will be faced with a large variety of development tasks and engage with the customers. Visits to construction sites with huge contracting machines can be a part of the job, and give you a first-hand impression of the context we are working in.

Key points on your profile:

• Study Software Engineering, Computer Science or similar and ready to start internship in February 2027
• Programming experience in C# or a similar object-oriented language (Java, C++)
• Understanding of software design principles, e.g. SOLID, design patterns and clean code
• Hungry to learn and eager to bring new ideas and methods from your studies into a real product
• Curious about AI and keen to learn how to use it in your workflows
• Able to communicate professionally in English, both spoken and written
What we offer

We can promise a versatile job in a truly great culture, with a modern setup and plenty of opportunities to expand your repertoire in software.

• 25 colleagues in our Product Development department, who are ready to onboard you swiftly
• A chance to become a core member of a growing company at a very interesting point in time
• Great team spirit and colleagues who are ready to go the extra mile to get success
• Meaningful technical challenges that solve real problems
• Delicious lunch buffet and social events
• Facilities and interior design that facilitate collaboration and creativity
• Compensation
How to apply

Send your CV and letter of motivation in .pdf format.

About us

Unicontrol's focus is to use advanced technologies and make them as user-friendly as possible. Our technology is based on high precision sensors installed on earthmoving machines and controlled by our advanced software. At present, we are around 65 employees, and we are active in more than 25 countries around the world through partners. Unicontrol is part of Odense Robotics national cluster organisation for robot, drone and automation businesses.

jobs.occupation: Data Platform Engineer – Offshore Wind Industry
jobs.description:
Are you passionate about building and running reliable, scalable and secure cloud data platforms? Do you want to work in the offshore wind industry, where your engineering skills will help secure a sustainable future based on renewable energy? Then keep reading: Cadeler is looking for a Data Platform Engineer with your skills and interests!

Cadeler is a global partner in the offshore wind industry, specializing in wind farm construction and maintenance. Our industry is more relevant than ever and plays a critical role in the energy transition, with a strong long-term outlook. As our industry continues to develop, so do we!

We are now looking for a Data Platform Engineer to help build, automate and operate our cloud data platform, ensuring that trusted and well-governed data is available for analytics, reporting and operational decision-making.

**What will you do?

**As our Data Platform Engineer, you will design, build and operate the technical foundations of Cadeler's data platform on Snowflake and Azure. You will work with business teams, application owners, IT and information security to integrate source systems, automate data pipelines and make reliable data available for analytics and reporting.

**Your Main Tasks Include

**

• Design, build and maintain data pipelines from various source systems, using managed ingestion tools such as Fivetran and custom Python where connectors fall short

• Orchestrate and schedule pipelines, handle dependencies, retries and backfills, and manage Snowflake warehouse sizing and compute cost

• Own CI/CD and source control in Azure DevOps: branching strategy, PR reviews, automated deployments and environment promotion (dev, test, prod), with database objects and infrastructure managed as code

• Design and implement dimensional data models (facts, dimensions, star schemas, slowly changing dimensions) across raw, staging, integration and mart layers

• Set up pipeline monitoring, anomaly detection and alerting, and troubleshoot and resolve incidents in production

• Deliver curated, performant datasets and semantic-ready measures so departments can build reports in Power BI

**To Succeed In This Role

**Being part of the Cadeler community means having a natural interest in and care for the environment, and in our shared mission to speed up the green energy transition. Environmental considerations and the safety of our people and the planet will be a key priority in your daily work.

We are looking for an innovator with a solution-oriented mind, who thrives in a fast-paced environment with many different interfaces.

We think you will be a good match if you have:

• A university degree in a relevant area such as computing, statistics or mathematics

• 3+ years of hands-on experience as a data engineer or data platform engineer

• Proven experience designing, building and operating production data pipelines

• Advanced SQL skills and strong Python skills for data processing, automation and tooling, and experience with dimensional modelling

• Hands-on experience with Snowflake (warehouses, RBAC, storage and compute management, cost control) and the Azure ecosystem

• An understanding of data security, governance and access control principles, as well as ability to define and write logic that transforms raw data into useful, interpretable, business-driven datasets

• Fluent spoken and written English

**Come work with us!

**By becoming a Cadeler employee, you will be part of a rapidly growing company with a diverse and energetic team. We offer an exciting position focused on delivering excellence in the face of interesting new challenges, within a positive and rewarding work environment in an international company with great development possibilities.

Cadeler is headquartered in Copenhagen, with offices in Vejle, Norwich, Rotterdam and Taipei, as well as colleagues working offshore aboard our fleet of Wind Farm Installation Vessels (WFIV).

Meet some of our colleagues here: https://www.cadeler.com/career

**Apply

**Use the APPLY button to apply for this position. For data protection purposes, applications are only accepted via the link and are assessed continuously until we find the right candidate, so please don't hesitate to send in your application as soon as possible and no later than the 6th of November.

If you have any questions about the position, and/or for practical matters, please contact peopleandculture@cadeler.com.

_Pandora jewellery is loved by millions. Do you want to help keep the company as strong as the love its products attract? ... If so, this could be the opportunity you’ve been looking for!

_**_Pandora sells more jewellery than any brand in the world, at a gross margin of around 80 percent, among the strongest in consumer goods. That strength is what lets the brand keep creating, designing, crafting and showing up for the people who wear it, and what earns the trust of the investors who back it. Guarding it, piece by piece and collection by collection, is what this newly created role is for. We deliver on our promises, and precious metals at multi-year highs are testing every jewellery maker's discipline right now. The brands that keep their craft and their strength through it will set the pace. That is the work, and it starts immediately.

_**Pandora's success is built on product: design that powers both the love for the brand and the profit that sustains it, and an assortment where every piece earns its place, in the stores and in people's hearts. You will build product profitability governance with our Product organization: what enters the assortment and on what threshold, what leaves it and when, and how design, cost, price and mix add up to a portfolio that earns steady love from millions.

You lead through mandate and the forums you chair, not headcount: the team is deliberately senior and flat, and your counterparts are the CPO leadership team, Merchandising, Revenue Growth Management, Craft & Supply finance and the CFO office. Your work is in front of the Executive Leadership Team every cycle, at the center of the company's strategic agenda.

**What You Will Do

**

• Design and chair the product gate and lifecycle forums, moving with the assortment cycle: thresholds set, decisions evidenced, follow-through visible, and a line where every piece earns its place.

• Own the numbers behind what every product costs and earns, hands-on in the cost and BI systems, and build the story behind them, told at Executive Leadership and investor standard.

• Partner Product Strategy, Merchandising, pricing and Craft & Supply finance on how design choices become cost, how whole product families keep earning as they grow, and the link between what we choose to sell and what we charge.

• Hold the finance position with senior product stakeholders on thresholds and lifecycle decisions, and keep the partnership strong while you do it.

• Direct a product finance analyst on content and draw on a shared analytics bench built for exactly this work. Contribute to building agentic capabilities to expand the value you deliver.

**What Is Needed To Succeed

**

• 10+ years in product or gross margin finance from vertically integrated retail or consumer goods; you have run a costing or product-profitability function, not only analyzed one.

• Hands-on analytical depth that has stayed recent: you build and defend margin baselines yourself, and master data is familiar ground.

• A track record of building governance that held: gates or lifecycle forums with thresholds that survived contested, sponsored proposals.

• Credibility in front of a CFO and a CPO in the same meeting.

**Who You Are

**

• A self-starter: you break the ice on work nobody has owned before and bring structure where there was none.

• You develop and defend your own point of view, and you change it when the evidence says so.

• Consumer-centric: you know growth comes from products people love and a brand they think of first, and you read margin through that lens. Multipliers, not mechanical levers.

• You believe finance is a strategic copilot to the business, in the room when plans are made, not after they are priced. And you see it as the essential guardrail that keeps a company strong enough to be trusted, by the people who wear the jewellery and the investors who back it.

• You can have difficult conversations respectfully: holding strategic financial realities against a proposal someone loves, and keeping the relationship.

• People-centric and a collaborator: you build capability in others and win as a team across functions.

Reporting into the Sr Director, Global Product & Marketing Finance, you will join a small, senior team at the center of a chapter Pandora is building on design, brand and the discipline underneath them, with a mandate sponsored from the top of the company, the room to build, and a market that will not wait.

**Additional Information

**Global Career Band 4A - Senior Manager.

Hybrid Working Flexibility – 3 days in office per week

Location Copenhagen; Global scope.

English is our working language; Danish is not required.

Did we get your attention?   We process applications on a continuous basis, which is why we encourage you to send your application as soon as possible. You can also read more about Pandora on our corporate site www.pandoragroup.com.

Icing on the cake

You will be working out of our beautiful Head Office in Copenhagen V, established in 2016 and designed to unite and inspire our teams. Besides our beautiful interior design, we are also proud of our LEED Gold Certification for Energy and Environmental Design. This means that we use as few natural resources as possible and that we use them with respect. The result is a professional and dynamic space that is unique, comfortable and inspirational – and delivers a true Pandora experience to anyone who works here or comes to visit.

**About Pandora

**Pandora is the world's largest jewellery brand, specialising in the design, crafting and marketing of accessible luxury jewellery made from high-quality materials. Each piece is created to inspire self-expression, allowing people to share their stories and passions through meaningful jewellery. Pandora jewellery is sold in more than 100 countries through 7,000 points of sale, including more than 2,800 concept stores.

Headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, Pandora employs around 39,000 people worldwide and crafts its jewellery with 100% recycled silver and gold. Pandora is committed to leadership in sustainability and has set out to halve greenhouse gas emissions across its value chain by 2030. Pandora is listed on the Nasdaq Copenhagen stock exchange and generated revenue of DKK 32.5 billion (EUR 4.4 billion) in 2025.

At Pandora, we believe that creating an inclusive and diverse workplace and reflecting societal diversity in our customer engagement is essential to delivering on our company purpose: to give a voice to people’s loves. We dedicate ourselves to fostering, cultivating and preserving a culture of inclusion and diversity where everyone feels respected and valued.

NORMAL has more than 1,000 stores across 14 countries. Twelve of these countries are supported from our warehouse in Hedensted, while the remaining two are supported from our warehouse in Horsens.

Our warehouse in Hedensted is an international workplace with around 60 different nationalities, and there is plenty to keep moving. We are looking for a Team Leader who can create the right conditions for people to succeed, while making sure our dayly picking operation runs smoothly.

You do not necessarily need a background in logistics to succeed in this role. What matters most is your ability to lead people, take responsibility and bring out the best in those around you.

**What You’ll Be Doing

**

• Leading, supporting and developing a team of pickers and picking coordinators

• Creating clarity, structure and direction in the daily operation

• Motivating and guiding your team through feedback, coaching and everyday support

• Planning manpower needs and managing schedules

• Recruiting and onboarding the right people for the team

• Following up on picking performance, safety and compliance with our standards

• Identifying opportunities for improvement and turning good ideas into practical solutions

• Recognising and celebrating the difference your team makes to the operation

• Working closely with other warehouse departments to keep things running smoothly

• Acting as a role model: being a visible and involved leader in the daily operation, ready to step in when needed

**Who are you?

**You are the kind of leader who enjoys seeing other people succeed. You understand that strong results are created by strong teams, and you care about giving people the support, trust and space they need to do a good job.

You are approachable, organised and able to create structure without making things unnecessarily complicated. You communicate honestly and clearly, stay calm when priorities change and are comfortable making decisions when things get busy.

You do not have to know everything from day one. You are curious, open to learning and willing to develop both yourself and your team. You ask questions, listen to different perspectives and are not afraid to challenge the usual way of doing things when there is a smarter one.

At NORMAL, everyone has an important role to play. As a Team Leader, you will need to take ownership of your area, involve your team and follow things through. You give credit where it belongs, focus on the impact your team creates and help make their contribution visible.

You lead from the front and are not afraid to get involved when needed. At the same time, you know that leadership is not about having all the answers or being the loudest person in the room. It is about setting the team up to succeed, acting with integrity and creating results together.

And while we take the work seriously, we do not always take ourselves too seriously. There should be room for humour, spontaneity and a good laugh during the shift.

**We Also Expect That You

**

• Have experience leading a tea, ideally within picking, logistics or warehousing

• Have experience with a Warehouse Management System or similar tools, which would be an advantage

• Communicate confidently in English, both spoken and written

**Why NORMAL?

**At NORMAL, things move quickly, and there is rarely a long way from a good idea to action.

You will become part of an international operation with colleagues from around 60 different nationalities and a logistics centre that plays an important role in keeping our stores running across 12 countries.

You will have the opportunity to make a real difference, both to the daily operation and to the people around you. We believe in giving people responsibility and the freedom to find solutions, rather than expecting everything to be done in one particular way.

You will join a down-to-earth workplace where people help each other, share ideas and keep raising the bar. We do not expect every idea to work the first time. We expect people to try, learn, adjust and keep moving forward.

And if you can help create a team where people know what matters, feel trusted to do their job and enjoy coming to work, then you may be exactly the leader we are looking for.

**Practical information

**Location: Our logistics centre in Hedensted

Working hours: Full-time, 37 hours per week

Shift: Dayshift, 07.00-15.00

We hold interviews on an ongoing basis and hire when we find the right match.

If you have any questions about the role, please contact Picking Manager Ivan Donda at ivadon@normal.dk.

If you are ready to lead with energy, create direction and help your team succeed, we would love to hear from you.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Physics-Informed Machine Learning for Greenland’s Firn Tipping Point - DTU Space
jobs.description:
Are you interested in turning natural phenomena into equations and code, and then applying them to big open questions in climate science? If so, we are looking for a PhD student with a background in physics and/or mathematics to help predict when Greenland’s porous near-surface firn layer, which currently stores much of the ice sheet’s meltwater, loses that capacity, and what that means for sea-level rise.

You will build models that combine physics, machine learning, and satellite data, and apply them to climate scenarios from the EU’s Destination Earth initiative. You will join a diverse and collaborative group at DTU Space and develop skills in scientific computing and machine learning that are valued in both research and industry. No prior experience in glaciology or climate science is needed; we will help you learn the field.

Responsibilities and qualifications
In the FirnTip project, you will develop a framework that predicts when and where Greenland’s firn stops being able to store meltwater, a possible climate tipping point. You will work closely with your supervisors at DTU Space as well as international partners. 

Your main tasks will be to:

• Identify which climate factors control when firn stops absorbing meltwater
• Combine satellite-derived firn density with firn models (data assimilation)
• Develop machine-learning models (e.g., graph neural networks) that obey physical conservation laws.
• Detect early-warning signals of tipping points in future climate scenarios
• Spend 3-6 months aboard visiting international partners, planned in collaboration with you
• Take part in teaching and knowledge-sharing as part of the DTU PhD program
To do well in the role, we think you need:

• A master’s degree in physics, mathematics or a field with a comparable mathematical foundation
• Experience writing scientific code, e.g., from your thesis or projects
• Good knowledge of at least one of: differential equations, numerical methods, statistics, or machine learning
• Good written and spoken English
Experience with glaciology, remote sensing, or machine learning is not required.

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education.

Assessment
The assessment of the applicants will be conducted by Senior Researcher Sebastian B. Simonsen (DTU), Researcher Kirk M. Scanlan (DTU), and Senior Researcher Anja Rutishauser (GEUS) using common criteria for all applicants. Shortlisted applicants will have a structured interview, possibly including a short computational exercise. If you meet most, but not all, of the qualifications, please still apply. Let us know if you need any adjustments to the recruitment process. 

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures

The start date is February 1st or soon thereafter.

The position is a full-time position.

The period of employment is 3 years.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information 
Further information may be obtained from Senior Scientist Sebastian B. Simonsen, ssim@dtu.dk. Questions about the project or the application are welcome. 

You can read more about our DTU Space cryosphere research at https://www.space.dtu.dk/english/research-divisions/geodesy-and-earth-observation/research-areas/cryosphere

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 29 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time). 

Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
• A one-page description of a computational or mathematical project you have done (e.g., your MSc thesis): the problem, your methods and your own contribution.
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. 

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates, irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background, are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

You will join the Cryosphere Research Group in the Geodesy and Earth Observation Division at DTU Space, Lyngby Campus. We use satellites, models and on-the-ground measurements to understand how ice sheets and glaciers are changing and what this means for sea level, in projects for ESA and the EU. Our group is international and collaborative, and we value curiosity, good supervision and a healthy work-life balance. 

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Researcher in Process Modelling, Integration and Techno-Economic Analysis of Reversible Solid Oxide Electrolysis and biomethanation systems
jobs.description:
Applications are invited for a two-year postdoctoral position in process systems engineering at the Department of Biological and Chemical Engineering, Aarhus University, Denmark.

The successful applicant will contribute to a collaborative research and demonstration project focused on integrating reversible solid oxide electrolysis and fuel-cell operation with biogas production, biological methanation, and heat recovery. The research will combine process simulation, system integration, optimisation, and techno-economic analysis to evaluate flexible operation and support the scale-up of the technology.

Expected start date and duration of employment
This is a two year position from 1st of February 2027 or as soon possible. 

Job description
The successful applicant will contribute to a collaborative research and demonstration project focused on integrating reversible solid oxide electrolysis and fuel-cell operation with biogas production, biological methanation, and heat recovery. The advertised position has become available through an Energy Technology Development and Demonstration Programme (EUDP) Project from the Danish Energy Agency, called DyneMe. The project aims to demonstrate how a 300 kW second-generation Dynelectro electrolyser unit can boost biogas methane production from existing feedstock, maximise energy efficiency and provide grid-balancing capabilities through dynamic electrolyser load and when relevant fuel cell operation. The research will combine process simulation, system integration, optimisation, and techno-economic analysis to evaluate flexible operation. 

The main tasks include
• Developing process models, for all core unit operations, in Aspen Plus or comparable process-simulation software.
• Establishing mass and energy balances for electrolysis, fuel-cell operation, anaerobic digestion, biochemical methanation, biogas processing, steam production, and heat recovery.
• Evaluating the interaction between variable hydrogen production and biological hydrogen uptake.
• Identifying and evaluating heat-integration opportunities between the solid oxide system and the biogas facility.
• Simulating representative operating conditions, including part-load operation, hot standby, and SOEC and SOFC operating modes.
• Combining process-model results with time-series or dispatch models to assess operation under variable electricity prices, renewable-electricity availability, biogas production, and heat demand.
• Conducting techno-economic, sensitivity, and uncertainty analyses.
• Participating in regular project meetings and present the modeling activities.
Your profile
Applicants should hold a PhD in chemical engineering, process engineering, energy engineering, biochemical engineering or similar.

The successful candidate is expected to have 
• A strong background in process modelling, thermodynamics, mass and energy balances, and chemical or energy-process design.
• Extensive experience with Aspen Plus, Aspen HYSYS, or comparable process-simulation software.
• Experience in developing, analysing and validating models of chemical, biochemical, electrochemical, or energy-conversion processes.
• Experience with process integration, including pinch analysis and heat exchanger network design.
• Documented experience with techno-economic analysis, including sensitivity and uncertainty analysis.
• Experience with quantitative data analysis and a relevant programming or numerical-computing environment, such as Python or MATLAB.
• The ability to work independently, structure a complex modelling problem, document assumptions, and deliver results according to project deadlines.
• Documented ability to have scientific results of high quality published in peer-reviewed journals
• Excellent written and spoken English.
• Good communication and collaboration skills and an interest in working in an interdisciplinary project involving both academic and industrial partners.
Experience in one or more of the following areas will be considered an advantage
• Dynamic process simulations
• Mathematical optimisation 
• Development of surrogate models
• Electrolysis, fuel cells, hydrogen production or other electrochemical processes
• Biogas production, anaerobic digestion, biological methanation
Who we are
Department of Biological and Chemical Engineering (BCE) was established on January 1, 2021 in connection with Aarhus University’s reorganization of the engineering area. The department employs around 260 people and is responsible for research and education within the department’s scientific areas. We educate both Bachelors and Masters of Science in Engineering and around 825 students are enrolled in our study programs. Furthermore, we also offer an ambitious PhD program. Our PhD students have high academic ambitions and deliver high-quality results for both the private and the public sectors.

At the Department of Biological and Chemical Engineering, focus is on living systems, the biology of organisms, efficient production, and transformation of chemicals, materials and energy. We translate knowledge within biotechnology, food technology, environmental technology, chemical engineering, industrial biotechnology, medical biotechnology and electrochemical engineering, and more into new technologies and value-creating solutions that can also be used in the business community.

Many of our research and development activities are based on companies' specific innovation needs or specialist application areas. Close collaboration with the public sector and private businesses ensures that the knowledge and technology generated in the department's research environments has a clear anchoring in reality and benefits the surrounding society. We also provide research-based public sector consultancy and advice on technology in agriculture and food. 
BCE has strong research sections in Chemical Process Engineering and Bioprocess Engineering, among others. The successful candidate will be working within the Microbial Conversion Technologies and the Sustainable Process Systems Engineering groups.

What we offer 
• the opportunity to be part of a team developing novel technologies for sustainable fuels and make a high impact in solving climate change issues. 
• a well-developed research infrastructure, laboratories and access to shared equipment, software and databases 
• an exciting interdisciplinary environment with many national, international and industrial collaborators
• a research climate encouraging lively, open and critical discussion within and across different fields of research
• a work environment with close working relationships, networking and social activities
• a workplace characterised by professionalism, equality and a healthy work-life balance. 
Place of work and area of employment 
The place of work is Gustav Wieds Vej DK-8000, and the area of employment is Aarhus University with related departments. 

Contact information
For further information, please contact: Assoc. Prof. Michael Vedel Wegener Kofoed, mvk@bce.au.dk, +4593521051.

Deadline
Applications must be received no later than 27th of November.

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self. 

Formalities and salary range
Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

Aarhus University also offers a Junior Researcher Development Programme targeted at career development for postdocs at AU. You can read more about it here.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

It’s an exciting time to join Tactile. We're a diverse team of storytellers, puzzle enthusiasts, and casual mobile game creators. In more recent years, we have been scaling fast, in large part thanks to the success of a little game called Lily’s Garden. Now we’re on a mission to solidify our position as one of the leaders in creating out-of-the-ordinary casual puzzle games.

With more than 350 talented individuals, we are a mix of over 50 nationalities and 43% women. We truly appreciate the richness of different experiences and perspectives that Tactilers bring to the game. This is why we foster a lean organisational culture, in which each individual is encouraged to take responsibility, be open, and grow in their own way. We pride ourselves on cultivating a studio environment that avoids crunch, fosters your skills regardless of your discipline, and provides a space for you to be creative alongside other passionate and invested storytellers.

**🚀 Your Role & Impact

The Core team builds the internal tools behind Tactile own LiveOps, Marketing and Data operations, the backbone of our studio. We're looking for a second Product Designer to join Joy and our engineers in designing business-critical tools that every team at Tactile depends on.

**

**What We’re Looking For

**

• You care more about the end product than about design process, and you thrive working across disciplines

• Comfortable contributing directly to projects via PRs to improve designs or UX without waiting for programmers to implement them

• Experience in designing with Claude Code or similar agentic tools

• Real openness to agentic workflows, without an "AI produces slop" mindset

• Comfort prototyping in code, or a strong drive to learn
